proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6251 dākṣiṇa specifically gives Prakrit dāhiṇa/ḍāhiṇa ‘right’, Old Awadhi dā̆hina, Hindi dā̆hinā and Braj dahino, plus Hindi dā̃yā explained by crossing with vāma ‘left’. The h-bearing and contracted y-forms therefore belong to this long-vowel derivative rather than automatically to bare dakṣiṇa; local vowels, endings and loss of nasalization are qualified. No specific contact donor is established.

These y-bearing forms fit loss of intervocalic m with variable nasalization and v→b; unmarked nasalization and local final vowels remain qualified. Retained-m bama/bāmā and the h-bearing behiya are not silently grouped here.
